candidates.explanation: Cohesive labels capability with only route glue in app, direct local-store CRUD, correct RSC/GET/Action channels, server-derived auth plus RLS, and private row mapping. No rubric penalties.

Uses the correct runtime channels and avoids speculative ports or operation wrappers. Colocation and server-internal isolation are only partial because behavior is split between app and a generic lib bucket, and the repository is not explicitly server-only. The generic lib bucket incurs the fourth penalty.

Runtime channels, authentication, authorization, and private mapping are coherent. However, labels behavior is scattered across architecture-wide roots and routed through boundary/use-case entries despite being simple CRUD. The generic universal boundary and mandatory layered structure incur penalties.

Correctly separates RSC reads, browser GET reads, and Server Action writes, with explicit server-side auth and private provider mapping. It fails the small-CRUD architecture criteria by scattering the capability across many layer roots and adding a speculative repository port plus one forwarding use-case file per operation.
